definitions.explanation: The number three. An important number in Japanese culture, appearing in many expressions and traditions. Combines with counters in straightforward ways.

examples.japanese: {三|さん}{時|じ}に{会|あ}いましょう。
{三|さん}{人|にん}{家族|かぞく}です。
この{本|ほん}は{三|さん}{冊|さつ}あります。
examples.english: There are three of these books.

examples.japanese: {三|さん}{年|ねん}{前|まえ}に{日本|にほん}に{来|き}ました。
examples.english: I came to Japan three years ago.

examples.japanese: {三|さん}{月|がつ}は{春|はる}の{始|はじ}まりです。{花|はな}がきれいです。
examples.english: March is the beginning of spring. The flowers are beautiful.

notes: The native Japanese reading is {三|みっ}つ (mittsu) when counting things with the つ counter. In most other counter combinations, さん is used: {三|さん}{月|がつ} (sangatsu, March), {三|さん}{本|ぼん} (sanbon, three long objects). Note how the counter {本|ほん} becomes ぼん after さん.
